tool_signatures.name: asset_upload_url
tool_signatures.description: Get a signed upload URL for a local file (so users do not have to host video / image / audio elsewhere before passing video_url to autonomous_edit). Body: { fileName, fileType?, contentType?, projectId? }. Returns { uploadUrl, fileUrl }; PUT the file bytes to uploadUrl, then pass fileUrl to autonomous_edit as video_url / in assets[].

tool_signatures.name: autonomous_edit_streaming
tool_signatures.description: Same as autonomous_edit but consumes the SSE event stream from the backend. Returns the final terminal result; per-step events (status, thinking, tool_call, tool_result, background_job_completed) are emitted as MCP progress notifications when the client supports them. Use for long-running briefs where users expect live progress.

tool.description: The tool to run. Keep as 'autonomous_edit' for natural-language prompts.

prompt.description: Natural-language description of the desired edit or creative brief. The backend planner decomposes it into canonical actions (viral clips, captions, reframe, export, …). Send the user's intent verbatim — do not pre-decompose.

project_id.description: Optional project id for tracking and continuity. Reuse the projectId returned by the first call for every continuation.

video_url.description: Optional public source video URL (HTTP/HTTPS: S3, Google Drive public link, Dropbox, direct MP4) for a new project. A local file path cannot be read directly: upload the file first (with the MCP server: call asset_upload_url, PUT the bytes to uploadUrl, then pass the returned fileUrl here).

assets.description: Optional input media assets. URLs must be public HTTP/HTTPS links; upload local files first (with the MCP server: asset_upload_url, then use the returned fileUrl).

url.description: Publicly accessible HTTP/HTTPS URL to the video, image, or audio asset.

captionTemplatePreset.description: Optional caption template to apply when (re)generating captions: a builtin slug (e.g. hormozi, mrbeast, viral-pop, karaoke, neon-pop, subtitle-bar) or a user-saved template id. With the MCP server, list_caption_templates lists the exact ids.
